newsitem.title: UK: Suicide pacts an upper-class thing - study.
newsitem.headline: Suicide pacts an upper-class thing - study.

text.p: The image of despondent young lovers leaping hand-in-hand off a cliff is outdated -- suicide pacts are for the older and better-off, British researchers said on Friday.
Martin Brown and Brian Barraclough of the University of Southampton analysed all reports of suicide pacts in England and Wales and found they were much less common than 35 years ago.
They found 124 people killed themselves in 62 pacts. Most -- 48 -- were between married couples and 58 chose to suffocate using car exhaust.
The mean age of those who died was 56 and nearly all were in the middle to upper social classes.

"People who commit suicide in a pact are more likely than those who commit suicide alone to be female, older, married and of a high social class," Brown and Barraclough wrote in a report in the British Medical Journal.
Most of those who died seemed to have planned their suicides carefully and in many cases one of those involved was seriously ill.
